# Benchmarks

## Per-example gradients

Median wall-clock time to get the gradient of every example in a batch: one
backward pass per example (`loop`), `vmap` over `grad`, and forward hooks
with a single backward pass. Single precision.
Measured on Apple M5 Max with torch 2.14.1.

| model | device | batch | loop (ms) | vmap (ms) | hooks (ms) | vmap speed-up | hooks speed-up |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| mlp 196-32-32-10 | cpu | 64 | 4.72 | 0.52 | 0.26 | 9x | 18x |
| gpt 2x64 | cpu | 64 | 58.90 | 8.12 | 7.00 | 7x | 8x |
| mlp 196-32-32-10 | cpu | 256 | 18.98 | 0.91 | 0.38 | 21x | 49x |
| gpt 2x64 | cpu | 256 | 229.82 | 19.88 | 18.81 | 12x | 12x |
| mlp 196-32-32-10 | mps | 64 | 18.59 | 1.20 | 1.14 | 15x | 16x |
| gpt 2x64 | mps | 64 | 158.07 | 7.97 | 3.60 | 20x | 44x |
| mlp 196-32-32-10 | mps | 256 | 67.96 | 1.09 | 1.01 | 62x | 68x |
| gpt 2x64 | mps | 256 | 434.42 | 20.86 | 4.56 | 21x | 95x |

## Single precision against double

Relative error of each quantity computed in float32, against the same
quantity in float64 on the CPU: the norm of the difference over the norm
of the reference. For the solves, the iteration counts are those of
conjugate gradient to a relative residual of 1e-6 in float32 and 1e-10 in
float64, and the residual is the true one of the float32 solution.

## Where time and memory go

Each stage on a batch of 256 sequences through the two-layer GPT of
width 64. Times are medians; the third column is the CPU time in units of the
first row, an ordinary training step. Peak memory and the operators' shares of
the time are from one run under `torch.profiler` on the CPU.
Measured on Apple M5 Max with torch 2.14.1.

| stage | cpu (ms) | mps (ms) | training steps (cpu) | peak on cpu (MiB) | busiest operators on cpu |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| forward and backward | 14.90 | 4.31 | 1.0 | 34 | bmm 40%, select 11%, mm 8% |
| per-example gradients, vmap | 23.16 | 17.51 | 1.6 | 177 | bmm 46%, select 11%, mm 7% |
| per-example gradients, hooks | 20.66 | 9.47 | 1.4 | 171 | bmm 47%, select 11%, as_strided 6% |
| gradient dot products with 16 queries, as sums over positions | 28.02 | 10.77 | 1.9 | 61 | bmm 40%, select 8%, addmm 5% |
| gradient dot products with 16 queries, materialised | 30.19 | 14.09 | 2.0 | 76 | bmm 35%, mm 16%, select 9% |
| Gauss-Newton-vector product | 49.91 | 9.92 | 3.3 | 41 | bmm 33%, select 9%, mm 8% |
| Hessian-vector product | 67.16 | 17.27 | 4.5 | 132 | bmm 34%, mul 10%, mm 8% |
| K-FAC factors | 21.79 | 16.20 | 1.5 | 64 | bmm 29%, mm 11%, exponential_ 10% |
| EK-FAC, factors and eigenvalues | 106.55 | 69.14 | 7.1 | 131 | bmm 34%, _linalg_eigh 19%, mm 11% |
| sparse projection of the gradients to 2048 | 14.66 | 22.36 | 1.0 | 116 | scatter_add_ 65%, mul 33%, div 1% |
| forward and backward, RMS norm fused | 27.22 | 5.10 | 1.8 | 34 | bmm 29%, mul 9%, select 8% |
| forward and backward, RMS norm from plain operations | 22.89 | 4.96 | 1.5 | 38 | bmm 29%, mul 9%, copy_ 8% |

## Training many models at once

Model updates per second at a batch of 64: one model with
`torch.optim`, and several stacked along a model dimension and trained through
`vmap`. The last column is the best of the stacked runs over the single model.
Measured on Apple M5 Max with torch 2.14.1.

| model | device | one at a time | 1 together | 8 together | 64 together | 512 together | gain |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| mlp 196-32-32-10 | cpu | 3,678 | 2,101 | 7,981 | 21,282 | 29,716 | 8.1x |
| gpt 2x64 | cpu | 206 | 148 | 288 | 331 | 309 | 1.6x |
| mlp 196-32-32-10 | mps | 1,044 | 881 | 5,510 | 19,346 | 24,095 | 23.1x |
| gpt 2x64 | mps | 315 | 231 | 1,412 | 2,157 | 2,045 | 6.9x |

## Preconditioning conjugate gradient

Iterations of conjugate gradient to a relative residual of 1e-8 against the
damped Gauss-Newton matrix, for three right-hand sides at once. The
preconditioners are the damped inverses of K-FAC, of EK-FAC, and of the true
matrix with the interactions between layers removed. Double precision, models
at their random initialisation. A star marks a solve that did not converge.
